newsitem.title: BERMUDA: CRICKET-NZ 204 FOR SIX AT TEA VS SRI LANKA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NZ 204 FOR SIX AT TEA VS SRI LANKA.

text.p: Offspinner Muttiah Muralitharan became the first Sri Lankan bowler to take 100 wickets in tests on Sunday during the third afternoon of the first cricket test against New Zealand.
Muralitharan, 24, reached the milestone when bowling New Zealand captain Stephen Fleming around his legs for 59 during the second session of play.
New Zealand went to tea on 204 for six in their second innings, holding an overall lead of 256 after dismissing Sri Lanka for 170 on Saturday. New Zealand made 222 in their first innings.
New Zealand resumed on 53 for one this morning but lost opener Bryan Young, for 62, and Matt Horne, 16, during the first session.
Fleming and Nathan Astle put together 75 for the fourth wicket before Muralitharan, playing in his 27th test, broke the partnership.
Fleming had looked most at ease on a pitch continuing to assist the spinners, hitting eight fours and one six to reach his 13th test half-century.
Muralitharan went wicketless in the first test last week in Dunedin but picked up three for 43 in New Zealand's first innings here to edge closer to his landmark.
He also has three so far in the second innings, at a cost of 54 runs, after having Chris Cairns snapped up by a bat-pad catch in close.
New Zealand wicketkeeper Adam Parore departed shortly before the tea break when he ran himself out for the second time in the match.
Nathan Astle, whose unbeaten 29 had been scored in 151 minutes, will resume after tea with Dipak Patel, who was on three.
